paper_metadata.title: Thermomechanical treatment influence on strength properties of vanadium alloys of V-Me(Cr, W)-Zr system at different temperatures

evidence.quote: The grain structure of V-Cr-W-Zr alloy after TMT-I with stabilizing annealing at 1000 ◦ С is heterogeneous ( Fig. 1 a). Grain sizes are in the range from several microns to several tens of microns. It was found that fine grains (up to 10 μ m) have an almost equiaxial shape, while larger grains are elongated in the rolling direction (RD) and are characterized by a non-equiaxiality coefficient (ratio of length of the major to minor axes) from 2 to 4.

attributes.size: coarse grains length 70-150 µm, width 10-40 µm; small grains up to 10 µm
attributes.morphology: coarse grains elongated in RD with gradient color indicating low-angle misorientations; interspersed with interlayers of small equiaxed grains

evidence.quote: Application of TMT-II with stabilizing annealing at Т = 1000 ◦ С leads to the formation of a non-uniform grain structure in V – Cr – W – Zr alloy ( Fig. 1 b). Coarse grains are elongated in RD, their length ranges from 70 to 150 μ m with a width of 10 to 40 μ m. A gradient color is observed inside such anisotropic grains, which indicates the presence of structural states with low-angle (discrete and/or continuous) misorientations. Large grains are interspersed with interlayers of comparable width, which consist of small (up to 10 μ m) grains of an almost equiaxed shape ( Fig. 1 b). There is no gradient color inside such small grains.

attributes.size: large grains length ≥50 µm, width 10-25 µm; fine grains length 5-15 µm, width ≤10 µm
attributes.morphology: large grains elongated in RD with non-equiaxiality coefficient 3-5; fine grains less anisotropic with non-equiaxiality coefficient ≤3; gradient color in largest grains

evidence.quote: In V – Cr – Zr alloy ( Fig. 1 c) after TMT-I with stabilizing annealing at 1000 ◦ С ( Fig. 1 a), anisotropy of the grain structure is observed in contrast to V – Cr – W – Zr alloy. Large grains are elongated in RD and reach a length of 50 μ m or more, and their width ranges from 10 to 25 μ m ( Fig. 1 c). Non-equiaxiality coefficient of such grains varies from 3 to 5. Fine grains are characterized by less pronounced anisotropy, non-equiaxiality coefficient does not exceed 3. Their sizes in RD are from 5 to 15 μ m, and their width does not exceed 10 μ m. In the largest grains a gradient color is observed.

attributes.size: large grains length several hundred microns, width 20-40 µm
attributes.morphology: large grains elongated in RD with gradient color indicating anisotropic internal structure

evidence.quote: The grain structure of V – Cr – Zr alloy after TMT-II with stabilizing annealing at T = 1000 ◦ С ( Fig. 1 d) is in many respects similar to V-Cr-W- Zr alloy after similar processing ( Fig. 1 b). Large grains elongated in RD reach a length of several hundred microns and their width ranges from 20 to 40 μ m. A gradient color is observed inside such anisotropic grains.
